BirchTateRational

24 times ζ(−1) is −2
Proved in Leanring 2One wheel at a time: squares, characters and the number 24

The Riemann zeta function at −1 is −1/12 (from Mathlib's Bernoulli values). The largest cycle on which every open position squares to 1 is 24 (UnitSquares24), and 24 times ζ(−1) is −2. This is the numerical side of the Birch–Tate formula for the rational numbers: the order of K₂ of the integers, 2, equals the size of w₂ times ζ(−1). K₂ is not in Mathlib, so only the numbers are stated. Deligne and Ribet (1980) proved that w₂ times ζ(−1) is a whole number for every totally real field; this node is the rational case of that, in numbers. Classical; the link from the wheel side (open positions squaring to 1) is the point here.

What it adds: UnitSquares24 finds the 24 on the wheels; this node shows it is the same 24 that clears the denominator of ζ(−1).

Published sources

  • J. Hurrelbrink, Birch–Tate conjecture, Encyclopedia of Mathematics — states the formula and its numerical example for the rationals: w₂ = 24, ζ(−1) = −1/12, K₂ of the integers of order 2
  • P. Deligne and K. Ribet, Values of abelian L-functions at negative integers over totally real fields, Invent. Math. 59 (1980), 227-286 — the integrality of w₂ times ζ(−1) for totally real fields, of which this is the rational case in numbers

w2_times_zeta
proved in Lean
The largest cycle length on which every open position squares to 1 is 24, and it times ζ(−1) is −2.
/-- **w₂ times ζ(−1) is −2.** There is a largest cycle length on which every
open position squares to 1; it is 24, and it times ζ(−1) is −2. -/
def w2_times_zeta : Prop :=
  ∃ m : ℕ, m ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ u : (ZMod m)ˣ, u ^ 2 = 1) ∧
    (∀ k : ℕ, k ≠ 0 → (∀ u : (ZMod k)ˣ, u ^ 2 = 1) → k ≤ m) ∧
    m = 24 ∧ (m : ℂ) * riemannZeta (-1) = -2
Rests on: UnitSquares24.units_square_one_iffBirchTateRational.zeta_neg_one
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.BirchTateRational.w2_times_zeta_step ↗
